title: Medical and Life-Support Protections — Schedule of Qualifying Conditions and Eligible Service
content:
Every protection offered under Medical and Life-Support Protections is a residential protection, available on Schedules RS, RT and REV, for a patient who is a full-time resident of the service address. The protections differ in the condition or the equipment that qualifies the patient.

## Eligible customer, schedules and household

| Protection | Customer class | Rate schedules | Patient's relation to the service address |
|---|---|---|---|
| Medical Emergency Certificate | residential | Schedules RS, RT and REV | patient is a full-time resident of the service address |
| Standard Medical Baseline Allowance | residential | Schedules RS, RT and REV | patient is a full-time resident of the service address |
| Heating and Cooling Medical Baseline Allowance | residential | Schedules RS, RT and REV | patient is a full-time resident of the service address |
| Combined Medical Baseline Allowance | residential | Schedules RS, RT and REV | patient is a full-time resident of the service address |
| Life-Support Registration | residential | Schedules RS, RT and REV | patient is a full-time resident of the service address |
| Critical Care Life-Support Registration | residential | Schedules RS, RT and REV | patient is a full-time resident of the service address |

## Qualifying conditions and recognised life-support equipment

| Protection | Qualifying condition or equipment | Equipment recognised as life support |
|---|---|---|
| Medical Emergency Certificate | any condition a practitioner certifies would be seriously aggravated by loss of electric service | not applicable |
| Standard Medical Baseline Allowance | use of a qualifying electrically powered medical device at home | not applicable |
| Heating and Cooling Medical Baseline Allowance | a condition requiring heating or air conditioning, such as multiple sclerosis, scleroderma, paraplegia or quadriplegia | not applicable |
| Combined Medical Baseline Allowance | both a qualifying medical device and a condition requiring heating or air conditioning | not applicable |
| Life-Support Registration | home use of life-support equipment that requires electric power | ventilator, oxygen concentrator, home dialysis machine, apnea monitor, suction machine, electric wheelchair or IV infusion pump |
| Critical Care Life-Support Registration | continuous dependence on life-support equipment where an interruption of more than two hours is life-threatening | ventilator, home dialysis machine, continuous oxygen concentrator or apnea monitor in continuous use |

## Notes on the schedule

- **Customer class and schedules are the same for all six protections.** None of the protections is listed for a business customer class or for a schedule other than RS, RT or REV.
- **The household test is the same for all six protections**: the patient must live at the service address full time.
- **The two life-support registrations recognise different equipment.** The Life-Support Registration list includes a suction machine, an electric wheelchair and an IV infusion pump; the Critical Care Life-Support Registration list does not, and it names the oxygen concentrator and the apnea monitor only where they are in continuous use.
- **The Combined Medical Baseline Allowance needs both elements** — a qualifying medical device and a condition requiring heating or air conditioning; either element on its own is the qualifying condition of the Standard Medical Baseline Allowance or of the Heating and Cooling Medical Baseline Allowance respectively.

### Hypothetical illustrations

- A patient living full time at the address uses an apnea monitor only at night. The apnea monitor is recognised life-support equipment for the Life-Support Registration; for the Critical Care Life-Support Registration it is recognised only when in continuous use.
- A patient's practitioner certifies a condition that would be seriously aggravated by loss of electric service, with no qualifying device or life-support equipment. Of the six qualifying conditions in the table, that description matches the Medical Emergency Certificate.
